subject: Post-call: CloudForge benchmark plan — latency/throughput A/B tests
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@cloudforge.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@cloudforge.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks + requested latency/throughput details

Thanks for the demo today — the team and I found the routing/fallback discussion helpful. A couple follow-ups from our side as we scope a bake/POC:

- Primary ask: we need a reproducible matrix of p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec comparing Redwood-hosted inference vs the hyperscaler endpoints we currently run (GCP CloudAI + HyperCloud managed endpoints).
- Important slices: short prompts (~30 tokens), medium (~256 tokens), long (~1024 tokens); both cold-start (no KV cache) and warm (after prefix caching).
- Also want to see throughput under 8, 32, 128 concurrent requests (tokens/sec and overall p95/p99).

Can you propose a concrete A/B test plan (one-pager) and schedule? If Redwood can show consistent p99 gains or cost parity at our throughput, that will accelerate procurement.

Attachments: sample request logs from our prod mirror.
[Attachment: cloudforge-prospect-logs.zip (application/zip)]

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync next week.

—Alex
Director of Platform Engineering, CloudForge
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@cloudforge.io>, Priya Singh <priya@cloudforge.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks + requested latency/throughput details

Alex — great to connect, and appreciate the detailed asks. High-level recap and proposed A/B plan below.

Recap from our call:
- Goal: side-by-side p95/p99 and tokens/sec across the three prompt lengths and cache states you outlined; measure both single-request latency and sustained throughput under concurrent load.
- Success criteria (from your notes): p99 <= 200ms for short prompts at 32 concurrent QPS; <10% cost delta vs hyperscaler at target throughput.

Proposed benchmark plan (attached: bench spec workbook):
1) Matrix: models (redwood-opt-13b, redwood-quant-13b), hyperscaler standard models (their 13b equivalent)
2) Prompt lengths: 30, 256, 1024 tokens; cache states: cold / warm
3) Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent sessions; measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and token cost per 1M tokens.
4) Runs: 3 steady-state runs per cell (5 minutes each) + cold-start burst tests (30s)
5) Instrumentation: we’ll capture raw request traces (latency buckets), kernel-level telemetry where possible, and token accounting to map to cost.

Owners & timeline:
- Karthik Iyer — lead on running lab and test harness (we’ll reuse the InferBench runner, add your request logs). Target: start 2026-11-30, deliver first pass 2026-12-03.
- Marissa Cole — validation, telemetry QA, and result write-up (p95/p99 analysis). Deliverable: benchmark readout + recommendation.
- Soojin — customer-facing recap, procurement checklist, and next exec brief.

Next steps for you: confirm target models (we can map equivalence if you provide the hyperscaler model IDs), and confirm whether we should include quantized variants for cost tradeoffs. I’ve attached a workbook with the test cells and a sample script we’ll run.

Attachments: cf-bench-specs.xlsx (contains matrix + instrumentation checklist)
[Attachment: cf-bench-specs.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

I’ll loop Karthik and Marissa on the scheduling email. Thanks — we’ll aim to keep the first pass tight so you get clear p95/p99 deltas.

—So
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudForge benchmark plan — action items + constraints

Fyi — forwarding Alex’s asks. Key internal action items and constraints for the lab run: 

Action items (priority):
- Karthik: stand up two parallel harnesses: Redwood-hosted runtime (default path) + hyperscaler client runner (we’ll call their public endpoints) using CloudForge logs as a replay source. Add flags to toggle cache state: --warm-cache --cold-cache.
- Include quantization variants: 16-bit float baseline + 8-bit quant for cost comparisons.
- Run wallclock and kernel telemetry to explain p95/p99 deltas (capture GPU queue times).
- Marissa: create the result template (CSV + short slide) highlighting p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec; include cost per 1M tokens assuming CloudForge’s current unit pricing (Alex will share).

Measurement specifics:
- Use 3 trials per cell; discard first warm-up minute for steady-state metrics. Calculate 95/99 using latency histograms; include 99.9th if any outliers.
- Pay attention to batching behavior — record average batch size and variance.

Constraints / customer asks:
- p99 target for short prompts: <= 200ms at 32 concurrency. If we can show median wins with small p99 improvements + cost parity, procurement is favorable.
- They will expect a short readout deck and a JIRA ticket tying results to procurement ops (link below).

Links / artifacts:
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/98765
- JIRA: SUP-6789 (CloudForge POC workstream)
- Bench spec attached in original mail.

Schedule: aim to run bench on 2026-11-30 with a 1-hour sync on 2026-12-03 to review preliminary numbers.

Please confirm if any infra pre-reqs are needed (special kernel builds, extra GPU quota).

—So
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@cloudforge.io>
